conventions.convention: The potential is Fε(s)=(s²−1)²/(4ε²), with fε(s)=(s³−s)/ε² and positive ε, κ and M. AC uses the L² metric; CH uses the mean-zero H⁻¹ metric and conserves mass.
A_h approximates −Δ. The finite-volume mass is cell-volume weighted and its stiffness sums only interior positive transmissibilities; prescribed zero boundary flux contributes no boundary penalty.
The conforming interval space is affine between centers x_i=(i−1/2)h and constant on boundary half-cells. Mass and both potential integrals are exact, without mass lumping.
The convex split is Fc(s)=s⁴/(4ε²)+s²/(2ε²), Fe(s)=s²/ε²−1/(4ε²), so Fε=Fc−Fe.
A_h† first projects onto the mean-zero subspace and then applies the inverse there. The Poincaré constant is fixed-mesh dependent; the one-cell mean-zero space is {0}.
The SAV input rⁿ is independent. The update does not impose rⁿ⁺¹=√(E₁,h(uⁿ⁺¹)+C₀), and its dissipated energy is κ〈A_hu,u〉_h/2+r².

Mesh-and-time convergence assumes the Axiom of Choice, fixed positive ε, κ and M, dimension one, initialization P_hu₀, and independent N,J→∞ with h=L/N and τ=T/J. Reconstructions use the new state on (t_n,t_{n+1}].
The modified-energy counterexample concerns an inequality alone; its scalar pairs are explicitly not claimed to satisfy the SAV update equations.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the no-flux finite-volume realization with interior-only stiffness, and the conforming interval realization with exact L² mass and potential integrals; both have self-adjoint nonnegative A_h approximating −Δ.

For either connected no-flux realization, A_h is self-adjoint and nonnegative, ker A_h=span{1}, ran A_h=X_h,0, and its restriction to X_h,0 is positive definite and invertible. Each fixed mesh has a finite Poincaré constant.

Under the algorithm's finite-dimensional hypotheses, with P_c,h convex and coercive and P_e,h differentiable and convex, both branches have a unique minimizer and satisfy their stated AC or CH recurrence. CH conserves mass. AC dissipates Mτ‖μⁿ⁺¹‖²_h and CH dissipates Mτ〈A_hμⁿ⁺¹,μⁿ⁺¹〉_h from the physical energy. The quartic split satisfies the required assumptions in both realizations.
For the conforming interval spaces, I_h and P_h are uniformly H¹-stable, their L² approximation errors on H¹ are bounded by Ch‖v′‖₂, P_hv→v in H¹ for every v∈H¹, and P_hg→g in L² for every g∈L².
The SAV linear system has a unique solution at every step, conserves the discrete mean, and satisfies Ẽ_h(uⁿ⁺¹,rⁿ⁺¹)+κ〈A_hδu,δu〉_h/2+(δr)²+Mτ〈A_hμⁿ⁺¹,μⁿ⁺¹〉_h=Ẽ_h(uⁿ,rⁿ).

concerns.concern: Step 4.1 says, “In the Allen–Cahn branch, step 1.2 gives δ=−Mτμⁿ⁺¹”. Step 1.2 proves existence and uniqueness; the recurrence is established in step 2.1. The argument is valid, but this explicit step citation points to the wrong step.

The Statement and Given paragraph omit the Axiom of Choice, although A1 explicitly assumes it and F2 uses the published absolutely-continuous-representative supplier, whose Statement requires it. The proof carries the assumption in its facts block; the standalone Statement should expose that qualification.
